Genetic covariance matrices from locus effects

Source: R/locus_G.R
indri_locus_G.Rd

The additive (G) and dominance (D) covariance matrices of a set of traits implied by the additive and dominance effects of individual loci, their allele frequencies and the linkage disequilibrium between them (Melo, Marroig and Wolf 2019, Eqs. 7-14). Each locus contributes through its vector of pleiotropic effects, so G and D show how the loci found by indri_gwas(), or by any other mapping method, build up the genetic covariance between the traits.

Usage

indri_locus_G(
  a,
  d = NULL,
  genotypes = NULL,
  p = NULL,
  lambda = NULL,
  ld = TRUE,
  traits_in = c("columns", "rows")
)

Arguments

a

Additive effects, loci by traits (a matrix, a numeric data frame, or a data frame with one column of locus names; a vector for one trait), or an indri_gwas scan (whose a, and d with dominance = TRUE, are used). Loci without an estimate are dropped.

d

Dominance effects, in the same layout as a; NULL for none.

genotypes

Individuals by loci, 0/1/2 dosages of the allele the effects refer to, for the allele frequencies and the linkage disequilibrium. May have more loci than a.

p

Allele frequencies, one per locus, instead of genotypes.

lambda

Linkage disequilibrium between the loci (loci by loci; the diagonal is ignored), instead of the estimate from genotypes.

ld

If FALSE, ignore linkage disequilibrium (only the per-locus sums).

traits_in

Where the traits are in a and d: "columns" (the default: one row per locus, one column per trait) or "rows".

Value

A list with G and D (traits by traits), alpha (the average effects, loci by traits), p and loci (the loci used).

Details

For locus j with allele frequency p_j (of the allele the 0/1/2 dosage counts; q_j = 1 - p_j), additive effects a_j and dominance effects d_j (vectors over the traits), the average effect is alpha_j = a_j + (q_j - p_j) d_j (Eq. 7), and

  • G = sum_j 2 p_j q_j alpha_j alpha_j' + sum_{j != x} 2 lambda_jx alpha_j alpha_x' (Eqs. 9-10),

  • D = sum_j (2 p_j q_j)^2 d_j d_j' + sum_{j != x} 4 lambda_jx^2 d_j d_x' (Eqs. 11-12),

where lambda_jx is the linkage disequilibrium between loci j and x. From an unphased genotype matrix it is the composite estimate lambda_jx = Cov(g_j, g_x) / 2 of the dosages.

Conventions for effects from other software

The formulas assume one convention for the effects; estimates from other packages have to be put on it, or G and D are wrong without any error.

  • Effect allele. a is the effect of one copy of the allele that the 0/1/2 genotypes count (half the difference between the two homozygotes), and p is that allele's frequency. GWAS software reports each beta for a named allele (for example A1 in PLINK 2's --glm output, ALLELE1 in regenie, allele1 in GEMMA): the genotypes must count that allele, or that locus's a must be negated. Check this per locus; tools differ in which allele they report.

  • Dominance coding. d is the deviation of the heterozygote from the midpoint of the homozygotes, which is what a regression on the dosage plus a heterozygote indicator (1 for genotype 1, 0 otherwise) estimates (as indri_gwas() does, and as the LL = +1, LS = 0, SS = -1 coding of lgsm_genotypes with its D column). Orthogonal or frequency-centred dominance codings (Cockerham's, for instance) estimate other quantities and must be converted first. Most GWAS software estimates no dominance: leave d = NULL.

  • Units. Effects in the units of the traits give G and D in those units squared. Standardised betas give matrices on the standardised scale.

  • Shape. Effects are loci by traits (one row per locus); a matrix with one row per trait needs traits_in = "rows". A data frame may carry one non-numeric column of locus names.

Loci are matched to the columns of genotypes, and to d, p and lambda, by name whenever both sides are named. Matching to genotypes by position warns, as does matching d by position when only one side is named.

References

Melo, D., Marroig, G. and Wolf, J. B. (2019). Genomic perspective on multivariate variation, pleiotropy, and evolution. Journal of Heredity 110, 479-493. doi:10.1093/jhered/esz011

See also

indri_gwas()

Examples

# one locus with effects on three traits
indri_locus_G(matrix(c(0.5, -0.2, 0.1), 1), d = matrix(c(0.3, 0, 0), 1),
              p = 0.4)$G
#>           [,1]     [,2]     [,3]
#> [1,]  0.150528 -0.05376  0.02688
#> [2,] -0.053760  0.01920 -0.00960
#> [3,]  0.026880 -0.00960  0.00480
